The music video for the original version of "Apologize" was created by filmmaker Aaron Platt in 2006, after the band had asked fans on Myspace to make one. It begins with Tedder writing the word "apologize" on a parchment letter with a needlepoint pen. What follows is interspersed footage of various different things, including: a woman reading the letter, Tedder singing the song while on the end of a handset, ink blots, the rest of the band performing and glass smashing.

An official video associated with the remix was filmed on September 19, 2007, and released in early October. The video premiered on VH1's Top 20 Countdown on October 27, 2007. The video was directed by Robert Hales and was shot in a recording studio showing OneRepublic performing the song. It also includes scenes from a New Year's Eve countdown party, starring actor Brian A. Pollack. In a third version of the video, also directed by Robert Hales and associated with the remix, Timbaland is portrayed remixing the song himself. A European version of the video features clips of the film Keinohrhasen, starring Til Schweiger. A Japanese version of the video was also made available for a short time. It features the same footage as the original but has more scenes from different camera angles. It also features footage of people falling and floating in the air in slow motion. The music video currently has 948 million views.

sections.heading: Chart performance
sections.wikitext:
"Apologize" was OneRepublic's breakout hit. In the United States, "Apologize" peaked at number two on the ''Billboard'' Hot 100 for four non-consecutive weeks. It spent 11 weeks at number three and 25 weeks inside the top 10 and peaked at number three for 10 weeks on the [[Hot 100 Airplay]]. It also topped the ''Billboard'' Pop 100 and became the third single from ''Shock Value'' to have topped the chart. It also became the album's first number-one single on the ''Billboard'' [[Adult Pop Songs|Adult Top 40]]. It is also the second consecutive single from ''Shock Value'' to reach number one on the US [[Mainstream Top 40]] radio. It became only the tenth song to sell over 5 million by May 2011 in the US.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://new.music.yahoo.com/blogs/chart_watch/74363/week-ending-may-8-2011-songs-rolling-in-the-dough/ |title=Week Ending May 8, 2011. In the UK, "Apologize" climbed to number 32 on the strength of digital downloads alone, and peaked at number three. The song spent 28 consecutive weeks in the top 40 and 13 weeks in the top 10. The song ended 2007 as the year's sixteenth biggest selling single in Britain.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/radio1/chart/singles2007.shtml|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081205090257/http://www.bbc.co.uk/radio1/chart/singles2007.shtml|title=Top 40 Singles of the Year 2007|work=BBC Radio 1 |publisher=[[BBC Music]]|access-date=December 30, 2007|archive-date=December 5, 2008}}</ref> In Australia, the single debuted at number 10 on the [[ARIA Charts|ARIA Singles Chart]], and peaked at number one. It stayed at the top for eight consecutive weeks, and was certified 4× Platinum by [[ARIA Charts|ARIA]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ariacharts.com.au/pages/charts_display.asp?chart=1U50|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071231022347/http://www.ariacharts.com.au/pages/charts_display.asp?chart=1U50|title=Top 50 Singles Chart – Australian Record Industry Association|website=Ariacharts.com.au|access-date=October 24, 2011|archive-date=December 31, 2007}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aria.com.au/pages/aria-charts-end-of-year-charts-top-100-singles-2007.htm|title=ARIA Charts – End Of Year Charts – Top 100 Singles 2007|publisher=ARIA|access-date=May 13, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=Steffen Hung|url=http://www.australian-charts.com/showitem.asp?interpret=Timbaland+presents+OneRepublic&titel=Apologize&cat=s|title=Timbaland presents OneRepublic – Apologize|website=australian-charts.com|access-date=October 24, 2011}}</ref> The song reached number one on both the [[Canadian Hot 100]] and [[RIANZ|New Zealand RIANZ Chart]]. It is the most downloaded single of all time in Australia and New Zealand. On ''Billboard''{{'s}} official [[European Hot 100 Singles]] chart, the song debuted at number 16, making it the highest debut chart position of any new act in the history of the chart. It later entered the top 10. The song went gold in Russia with 100,000 copies sold.<ref name="bare_url">{{cite web |url=http://2m-online.ru/news/detail.php?ID=5659 |title=Archived copy |website=2m-online.ru |access-date=9 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131002100728/http://2m-online.ru/news/detail.php?ID=5659 |archive-date=2 October 2013 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

sections.heading: Covers
sections.wikitext:
* Australian musician [[Natalie Gauci]] sang the song in the finale episode of the [[Australian Idol (season 5)|fifth season]] of ''[[Australian Idol]]'' in 2007.
* [[Luke Bryan]] covered "Apologize" on ''[[Doin' My Thing]].''<ref name="Luke Bryan Covers Apologize">{{cite web|url=http://music-mix.ew.com/2009/09/24/luke-bryan-onerepublic-apologize-exclusive/|title=Luke Bryan's country cover of OneRepublic's 'Apologize': Hear it exclusively on EW.com!|website=Music-mix.ew.com|access-date=March 11, 2022}}</ref>
* [[Kris Allen]] covered "Apologize" on the [[American Idol (season 8)|eighth season]] of ''[[American Idol]]''.
* Dutch symphonic metal band [[Within Temptation]] covered the song as part of their weekly radio promos for their 15-year anniversary show, ''Elements''. The song is also featured on their cover album ''[[The Q-Music Sessions]]''.
* Swedish alternative metal band [[All Ends]] covered the song on their album ''All Ends''.
* Canadian post-hardcore band [[Silverstein (band)|Silverstein]] covered the song on the ''[[Punk Goes Pop 2]]'' compilation album.
* On February 2, 2010, Soomo Publishing uploaded a parody version of this song, titled "Too Late to Apologize: A Declaration" to [[YouTube]], which has more than 14 million views as of February 21, 2025.<ref name="Too Late to Apologize: A Declaration">{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uZfRaWAtBVg|title=Too Late to Apologize: A Declaration|date=February 2, 2010 |via=[[YouTube]]|access-date=March 11, 2022}}</ref>
* Actor and singer [[Willam]] released a parody cover in 2013 titled "RuPaulogize" where she discussed her experiences and disqualification on the [[RuPaul's Drag Race (season 4)|fourth season]] of ''[[RuPaul's Drag Race]]''. The season winner [[Sharon Needles]] plays [[RuPaul]].
* Female country singer [[Kacey Musgraves]] and [[Pixie Lott]] have also covered "Apologize". 
*[[Taylor Swift]] covered this song on the [[Speak Now World Tour]] as a mashup with her songs “[[Back to December]]” and “[[You're Not Sorry|You’re Not Sorry]]”.
